summary: City council voted 5-1 for a 30-day moratorium to draft a data center ordinance amendment; aimed at a proposed Liberty Data Centers site.
Commissioners unanimously approved a one-year halt on accepting, processing and approving data center land-use applications in unincorporated Mesa County.

scope: data center; hyperscale >=10,000 sq ft; county-zoned areas
summary: Commissioners unanimously approved a six-month moratorium on hyperscale data centers in county-controlled areas pending an Ohio EPA/OKI water study.
45-day urgency ordinance barring approval of data center land-use permits; extension of up to 10 months 15 days was to be heard. Extension not confirmed.
Borough council voted 4-3 for a six-month data center moratorium near the Triboro Industrial Park.
Town council approved a one-year moratorium on data centers, solar, wind and battery storage while the plan commission reviews zoning.
Supervisors adopted Resolution 07.14.2026.01, a moratorium on data center applications for 180 days to prepare a curative zoning amendment.
City council resolution backing a data center moratorium through the end of 2026 while the joint planning commission drafts regulations.
City council voted 5-3 for a one-year moratorium on data centers larger than 50,000 square feet.
City council unanimously imposed a 45-day moratorium on approving new data center land-use applications at a special meeting.
Council voted 7-1 for a six-month pause on accepting new data center applications (upstream lists this as pending).
Council extended the 45-day urgency moratorium on 2026-09-30 by 22 months 15 days, to 2028-08-25, by the required four-fifths vote.
Council voted 8-0 on 2026-09-28 to extend the data center moratorium by another 180 days; new end date not published.
City council passed an ordinance prohibiting data centers within city limits after a proposed 3.5M sq ft campus was withdrawn.
Council unanimously adopted a permanent prohibition on high-energy data processing facilities (data centers, AI, crypto mining); server rooms exempt.
Commissioners voted 4-1 to add large-scale data center facilities to land development code prohibitions in unincorporated areas.

scope: data center; large load centers; all districts
summary: Commission voted 5-0 for Ordinance 26-1101, an outright prohibition on large load centers, specifically data centers, in all zoning districts.
Board of County Commissioners adopted an ordinance prohibiting data centers and associated facilities in the unincorporated county.
Commission unanimously adopted an ordinance prohibiting data centers in all unincorporated zoning districts.
Fiscal court unanimously banned data centers, landfills and large battery storage countywide; first permanent data center ban in Kentucky.
Council voted 3-0 to add Article XII to Chapter 17.11, permanently prohibiting data centers citywide; effective about 2026-10-16.
City council banned data centers in every zoning district; signed by the mayor 2026-06-18.

scope: data center; citywide; prior approvals exempt
summary: Council unanimously adopted on second reading a citywide data center ban; three previously granted approvals are not affected.
Town council adopted an ordinance prohibiting data centers in all zones.
Township adopted two ordinances banning all data center use township-wide.
Council unanimously passed Bill 26-011 banning data centers countywide; signed by the County Executive 2026-06-10.
Village adopted an outright ban on data centers, crypto mining, blockchain computing and supporting power plants in its zoning jurisdiction.
Borough council unanimously adopted Ordinance 27-2026 prohibiting data centers as a use (Chapter 195).

scope: data center; commercial zones; existing grandfathered
summary: Township committee unanimously removed data centers as a permitted use in commercial zones; existing facilities grandfathered.

scope: data center; >500 sq ft; server rooms exempt
summary: City council voted 3-2 to ban data centers (facilities over 500 sq ft housing servers); school/office server rooms exempt.
Township adopted an ordinance banning data centers (notice published 2026-05-11).
Council unanimously approved a rewritten industrial zoning code that writes data centers out of the code, following an earlier moratorium.

scope: data center; all districts; routine IT exempt
summary: Town council updated general and zoning ordinances to prohibit data centers in all districts; routine IT/telecom facilities excluded.
City amended its zoning code in early August to bar data centers with footprints over 20,000 sq ft (indefinite).
City council adopted a zoning amendment prohibiting data centers over 5,000 sq ft (researched by Moratorium Nation, excluded there as a permanent ban).

scope: data center; hyperscale; tribally owned and trust land
summary: Principal Chief Hoskin issued a ban on hyperscale data centers on tribally owned and trust land after a task force report.
Tribal council passed a permanent moratorium on data centers within Pyramid Lake Paiute homelands.
Tribe adopted a resolution banning data centers on tribal lands (Moratorium Nation dates it 2026-05-26).
Tribal Council voted 11-0 for Ordinance No. 158 (2026), an indefinite moratorium on data centers on EBCI lands.
